prompt: Which OSI layer is responsible for logical addressing and choosing the best path between networks?
explanation: The Network layer handles logical (IP) addressing and path selection. Data Link handles MAC addressing on the local segment, and Transport handles end-to-end delivery guarantees.

prompt: Which OSI layer establishes, manages, and tears down connections between applications, and provides port-based multiplexing?
explanation: The Transport layer (TCP/UDP) multiplexes conversations using port numbers and, in TCP's case, manages connection setup, flow control, and reliability.

prompt: What is the correct name for a Protocol Data Unit at the Data Link layer?
explanation: Data Link layer PDUs are called frames. Layer 3 units are packets, Layer 4 TCP units are segments (UDP units are datagrams).

prompt: When an application sends data down the OSI stack for transmission, what is this process called?
explanation: Encapsulation wraps data with each layer's own header (and sometimes trailer) as it moves down the stack. The receiving side reverses this through decapsulation.

prompt: A branch office network connects every workstation to a single central switch. What topology is this?
explanation: In a star topology, every node has its own link back to a central device. It's easy to troubleshoot, but the central device is a single point of failure.

prompt: In a full mesh topology, what is the main tradeoff for the redundancy it provides?
choices: It cannot support more than two devices
The number of required links grows quickly as devices are added, raising cost and complexity
It requires all devices to share one collision domain
It cannot be used with routed networks
explanation: Full mesh gives every device a direct link to every other device, which maximizes redundancy but scales poorly — the link count grows by n(n-1)/2 as nodes are added.

prompt: A data center design connects every leaf switch to every spine switch, with no direct leaf-to-leaf links. What is the main benefit of this spine-leaf architecture?
choices: It eliminates the need for IP addressing
It provides predictable, low-latency paths with consistent hop count between any two leaf switches
It removes the need for redundant power supplies
It allows unlimited VLANs without trunking
explanation: Spine-leaf ensures any server-to-server path crosses exactly one spine switch, giving consistent latency and high east-west bandwidth typical of modern data center traffic patterns.

prompt: A campus network uses a star topology within each building but connects the buildings together in a partial mesh for redundancy. What is this overall design called?
explanation: A hybrid topology combines two or more basic topologies. Here, star wiring inside buildings is combined with a mesh between buildings.

prompt: A user connects a wireless keyboard, mouse, and headset to a laptop over Bluetooth. What type of network is this?
explanation: A Personal Area Network covers a very short range around one person or device, typically using Bluetooth or similar short-range radio.

prompt: A city government links several municipal buildings across downtown using leased fiber it does not own end-to-end beyond city limits. What best describes this network's scope?
explanation: A Metropolitan Area Network spans a city or large campus footprint — larger than a single-building LAN but smaller than a WAN spanning regions or countries.

prompt: A company replaces static site-to-site VPN tunnels with a solution that centrally manages multiple branch connections and dynamically chooses the best underlying transport (MPLS, broadband, LTE) per application. What is this called?
explanation: SD-WAN abstracts and centrally manages WAN links across multiple transport types, steering traffic dynamically based on policy and link conditions rather than relying on static routing.

prompt: What is the defining characteristic of Software-Defined Networking (SDN)?
choices: It separates the control plane from the data plane so forwarding logic can be managed centrally
It replaces all physical switches with virtual machines
It eliminates the need for IP addressing
It is only usable inside a single vendor's hardware
explanation: SDN centralizes the control plane (path/policy decisions) in a controller, separate from the data plane (packet forwarding) still done in switches, allowing programmatic, centralized management.

prompt: A provider offers a virtual firewall, virtual router, and virtual load balancer that run as software instances instead of dedicated appliances. What concept does this describe?
explanation: NFV replaces purpose-built network appliances with virtualized instances of the same functions running on standard hardware or in the cloud, easing scaling and management.

prompt: In cloud networking, what is a VPC?
choices: A logically isolated private network segment within a public cloud provider
A physical router installed at the customer's edge
A type of cloud-based load balancer
A protocol for encrypting DNS queries
explanation: A Virtual Private Cloud is a customer-defined, isolated slice of a public cloud provider's network, with its own IP space, subnets, and routing, similar in concept to a private on-premises LAN.

prompt: An organization runs its ERP system in one cloud provider and its data analytics platform in a different cloud provider, with no on-premises component. What best describes this deployment?
explanation: Multi-cloud means using services from more than one public cloud provider. Hybrid cloud specifically mixes on-premises (private) infrastructure with public cloud resources.

prompt: A company wants a private, dedicated network connection from its data center to its cloud VPC instead of routing cloud traffic over the public internet. What kind of connectivity option is this?
choices: A cloud direct connection / private circuit to the provider
explanation: Cloud providers offer dedicated private circuits (such as AWS Direct Connect or Azure ExpressRoute) that bypass the public internet for more consistent latency, throughput, and security than a standard VPN.

prompt: Which two ports does traditional active-mode FTP use for control and data traffic, respectively?
explanation: FTP uses port 21 for the control channel (commands, authentication) and port 20 for the actual data transfer in active mode.

prompt: Why has Telnet largely been replaced by SSH for remote CLI administration?
choices: Telnet sends all traffic, including credentials, in cleartext
Telnet cannot reach devices on a different subnet
explanation: Telnet (port 23) transmits everything unencrypted, including login credentials, making it trivial to sniff on the wire. SSH (port 22) encrypts the entire session.

prompt: Which protocol is commonly used to transfer a router or switch configuration file to or from a device, and offers no authentication?
explanation: Trivial File Transfer Protocol (UDP port 69) is lightweight and unauthenticated, historically used for transferring firmware and configuration files on trusted management networks.

prompt: A user wants to read email from a phone and a laptop and see the same folder structure and read/unread status on both. Which protocol supports this, and why is it a better fit than the alternative?
choices: POP3, because it deletes messages after download
IMAP, because it keeps mail and folder state synchronized on the server
SMTP, because it is used for retrieving mail
SNMP, because it supports multiple device polling
explanation: IMAP (port 143) keeps messages and folder structure on the server and syncs state across multiple clients. POP3 (port 110) typically downloads and removes mail from the server, which breaks multi-device consistency.

prompt: Which protocol synchronizes device clocks across a network, and why does accurate time matter for network operations?
choices: NTP; accurate timestamps are essential for correlating logs and validating certificates
SNMP; accurate timestamps are needed for polling interface counters
TFTP; accurate timestamps are needed for firmware transfers
LDAP; accurate timestamps are needed for directory replication only
explanation: Network Time Protocol (UDP 123) keeps device clocks synchronized, which matters for correlating log and security events across devices and for time-sensitive certificate validation.

prompt: A Windows file server shares folders that clients access over the network using \\server\share paths. Which protocol and port does this rely on?
explanation: Server Message Block (SMB), on TCP port 445, is the protocol behind native Windows file and printer sharing.

prompt: A network needs at least 25 usable host addresses on a single subnet. Which CIDR prefix is the most efficient choice?
explanation: A /27 provides 32 total addresses, 30 usable, which comfortably covers 25 hosts without wasting as many addresses as a /26 (62 usable) would.

prompt: What advantage does VLSM (Variable Length Subnet Masking) provide over dividing a network into equal fixed-size subnets?
choices: It allows subnets of different sizes to be carved from the same address block based on actual host needs, reducing waste
It removes the need for a default gateway
It automatically encrypts traffic between subnets
It doubles the available address space
explanation: VLSM lets an administrator size each subnet to fit its actual number of hosts — a point-to-point WAN link might get a /30 while a user VLAN gets a /24 — instead of wasting addresses on uniform blocks.

prompt: Which of the following is entirely within the private, non-routable IPv4 address space defined by RFC 1918?
explanation: 192.168.0.0/16 is one of the three RFC 1918 private ranges. 172.32.0.0 is outside the 172.16.0.0/12 private block, 11.0.0.0 is public space, and 169.254.0.0/16 is the separate APIPA range.

prompt: What is the correct rule for using the :: shorthand when writing an IPv6 address?
choices: :: may be used any number of times in one address
:: may be used only once per address, replacing one or more consecutive groups of all-zero hextets
:: is only valid in link-local addresses
explanation: :: can compress one contiguous run of all-zero 16-bit groups, and only once per address — otherwise the number of compressed groups would be ambiguous.

prompt: What is the IPv6 loopback address, equivalent to 127.0.0.1 in IPv4?
explanation: ::1 (all zeros with a trailing 1) is the IPv6 loopback address, used by a host to test its own IP stack.

prompt: Which IPv6 address prefix range is reserved for multicast traffic?
explanation: ff00::/8 is reserved for IPv6 multicast. fe80::/10 is link-local, fc00::/7 is unique local, and 2000::/3 covers global unicast.

prompt: A company's mail flow depends on a DNS record that tells other mail servers where to deliver messages for its domain, including a priority value for multiple servers. Which record type is this?
explanation: MX (Mail Exchange) records specify the mail server(s) responsible for a domain, each with a preference value so senders know which to try first.

prompt: Which DNS record type resolves an IP address back to a hostname, and in which special zone does it live?
choices: A PTR record, in an in-addr.arpa reverse lookup zone
A CNAME record, in the forward lookup zone
An SOA record, in the root zone
An NS record, in the forward lookup zone
explanation: PTR records perform reverse DNS lookups (IP-to-name) and are stored in special in-addr.arpa (IPv4) or ip6.arpa (IPv6) zones.

prompt: An administrator publishes a DNS TXT record containing SPF information for a domain. What is the general purpose of a TXT record?
choices: It maps a hostname to an IPv6 address
It stores arbitrary text data, commonly used for domain verification and email authentication policies
It delegates a subdomain to another set of nameservers
It records the zone's serial number and refresh interval
explanation: TXT records hold free-form text and are widely used for things like SPF, DKIM, and domain-ownership verification, rather than for direct name resolution.

prompt: When a client's stub resolver asks a recursive DNS resolver to look up a name, and that resolver in turn queries a root server, then a TLD server, then the authoritative server on the client's behalf, what is this overall process called?
explanation: Recursive resolution means the resolver does the full chain of queries itself and returns only the final answer to the client, rather than handing back referrals for the client to follow.

prompt: A DHCP server hands out addresses from a defined pool of 192.168.10.50 through 192.168.10.200 for one subnet. What is this pool called?
explanation: A scope is the range of addresses a DHCP server is configured to lease out on a given subnet. Reservations pin specific addresses to specific MAC addresses within that scope.

prompt: Clients on a remote subnet need to reach a DHCP server that lives on a different subnet, but DHCP discovery messages are broadcasts that routers don't forward by default. What allows this to work?
choices: A DHCP relay agent (IP helper) configured on the router forwards the requests to the DHCP server
The clients must be manually assigned static addresses instead
DHCP reservations automatically cross subnet boundaries
NTP synchronizes the DHCP broadcast domains
explanation: A DHCP relay agent, typically configured on the router interface (ip helper-address), converts the client's broadcast into a unicast forwarded to the remote DHCP server and relays the reply back.

prompt: Match each protocol to its default port number.
explanation: FTP control uses 21 (data uses 20), Telnet 23, TFTP 69 over UDP, SNMP agent polling on 161, LDAP directory queries on 389, and SMB file sharing on 445.

prompt: An IPv4 address of 10.4.2.1 falls into which historical address class?
explanation: Class A covers first-octet values 1–126, with a default /8 mask — 10.x.x.x is a classic Class A range (and also happens to be the RFC 1918 private range for large networks).

prompt: Match each network appliance to its job.

pairs.right: Spreads client requests across multiple servers
Makes requests on a client's behalf, enabling caching and filtering
File-level storage shared over the network
Block-level storage that appears as a local disk to servers

explanation: A load balancer distributes traffic, a proxy sits between client and destination, NAS serves files, and SAN serves block storage for databases and virtualization back-ends.

prompt: A company deploys public DNS resolvers at many locations worldwide, all sharing one published address; a query is automatically routed to whichever location is topologically nearest the requester. What traffic type does this use?
explanation: Anycast lets one address route to the nearest of several servers advertising it — exactly the pattern public DNS resolvers use for performance. Multicast targets a subscribed group, not "nearest one."

prompt: A routing protocol update needs to reach every other router running that protocol on the segment, but not every host on the network. Which traffic type fits?
explanation: Multicast delivers to a specific interested group — routers participating in the protocol — without flooding every host on the segment the way a broadcast would.

prompt: A datacenter needs to run a single connector carrying many fiber strands at once between two high-density patch panels. Which connector type is designed for this?
explanation: MPO connectors bundle multiple fiber strands into one connector for high-density runs. RJ11 is a phone jack, F-type is coaxial, and BNC is a legacy twist-lock coaxial connector.

prompt: Two switches sit in adjacent racks and need a cheap, high-speed link between them. Which option avoids the cost of separate fiber and optical transceivers?
explanation: A DAC cable has transceivers built onto both ends of a fixed copper cable, giving high-speed short-distance links without buying separate fiber and optics — ideal for adjacent-rack connections.

prompt: A small branch office's network design merges the core and distribution layers into a single tier of switching, since the site is too small to justify three separate layers. What is this design called?
explanation: A collapsed core merges the core and distribution layers into one tier — appropriate for smaller deployments that don't need the full three-tier design.

prompt: A company deploys an application entirely on a provider's platform, writing and pushing only their own code — the provider manages the OS, runtime, and scaling. Which cloud service model is this?
explanation: PaaS hands you a platform to deploy code onto; the provider manages everything underneath it. IaaS would still require you to manage the OS yourself; SaaS would mean using someone else's finished application.

prompt: A network monitoring system watches traffic for suspicious patterns and sends an alert, but takes no action to stop it. What kind of system is this?
explanation: An IDS (Intrusion Detection System) monitors and alerts only. An IPS (Intrusion Prevention System) sits inline and can actively block traffic — the detect-vs-prevent distinction is the whole point of the question.

prompt: A site-to-site tunnel must carry a routing protocol that plain IPsec can't transport on its own, and the traffic inside also needs to be encrypted. Which combination BEST fits?
choices: GRE for the tunnel, wrapped inside IPsec for encryption
GRE alone, since GRE encrypts its payload
IPsec AH alone, since AH encrypts the payload
A plain HTTP tunnel with TLS disabled
explanation: GRE can tunnel protocols IPsec can't carry directly, but GRE provides no encryption on its own — so GRE-over-IPsec is the standard pairing. AH authenticates but does not encrypt; ESP is the piece that encrypts.

prompt: Which IPsec component is responsible for encrypting the packet payload (as opposed to only authenticating it)?
explanation: ESP encrypts (and can also authenticate) the payload. AH provides authentication and integrity only, with no encryption. IKE negotiates the keys ESP/AH then use.

prompt: A streaming company wants video to load from a server geographically close to each viewer instead of always crossing the internet to the origin. Which is the BEST fit?
choices: A load balancer inside one data center
explanation: A CDN caches content on edge nodes near users, cutting latency and origin load. A single-data-center load balancer spreads requests but doesn't move content closer to distant users.

prompt: On a congested WAN link, voice calls break up while a large file transfer runs. Which mechanism is designed to prioritize the latency-sensitive traffic so this stops happening?
explanation: QoS prioritizes chosen traffic classes (like VoIP) on a congested link so they aren't stuck behind bulk transfers. TTL is a packet hop counter; jumbo frames increase frame size and would not help voice latency.

prompt: Instances in a cloud private subnet need to download OS updates from the internet, but must NOT be directly reachable from the internet. Which cloud construct provides exactly this?
choices: An internet gateway attached directly to the subnet
explanation: A NAT gateway lets private-subnet instances initiate outbound connections without being reachable inbound — the cloud equivalent of home-router NAT. An internet gateway on the subnet would make the instances publicly reachable.

prompt: A network designer is documenting the pieces of an IPsec VPN. Which TWO of the following are components defined within the IPsec suite?
explanation: AH and ESP are both IPsec components (authentication-only and encryption, respectively). GRE is a separate tunneling protocol often paired with IPsec but not part of it; QoS and CDN are unrelated to IPsec.

prompt: A cloud architect is choosing which service models hand OS management to the provider rather than the customer. Which TWO service models leave the customer NOT responsible for patching the underlying operating system?
explanation: With PaaS and SaaS the provider manages the OS (and more). With IaaS the customer still patches the guest OS themselves, and on-prem bare metal is entirely the customer's responsibility.

prompt: A large multi-tenant data center has exhausted the ~4,000-VLAN ceiling of 802.1Q and needs to stretch Layer 2 segments across a routed backbone between sites. Which technology is designed for this?
explanation: VXLAN wraps Layer 2 frames in UDP with a 24-bit identifier (16M+ segments) and tunnels them across a Layer 3 backbone — used for data center interconnect and scaling past the 12-bit VLAN limit. STP and native VLANs don't address the ceiling.

prompt: In a Zero Trust Architecture, a request is evaluated by the policy engine and a decision is issued, then a gateway actually blocks or permits the traffic based on that decision. The gateway enforcing the decision is part of which plane?
explanation: In ZTA the control plane decides (policy engine/administrator) and the data plane enforces (policy enforcement point). The gateway gating traffic is the enforcement point — the data plane.

prompt: A company wants remote users to get both SD-WAN connectivity and a full stack of cloud-delivered security (firewall, secure web gateway, zero-trust enforcement) from a single edge service instead of backhauling traffic to headquarters. What describes this converged model?
explanation: SASE converges networking (SD-WAN) and security services into one cloud-delivered edge. SSE is the security-only subset of SASE; VXLAN and MPLS are transport technologies, not converged security.

prompt: A network team stores device configurations in a version-controlled central repository and uses templates to push changes, so every change is tracked and a bad one can be rolled back. What practice is this?
explanation: IaC treats network/device configuration like software: templates/playbooks, version control, drift detection, and rollback. The whole point is that a config change goes through the same review-and-revert discipline as code.

prompt: Which TWO OSI layers would a technician examine when a host has a valid IP address but cannot reach a service on a remote server that is confirmed running?
choices: Layer 3 (Network) — routing and reachability to the remote subnet
Layer 4 (Transport) — whether the destination port is permitted and listening
Layer 1 (Physical) — the link is already confirmed up
Layer 7 (Application) — the service is confirmed running
Layer 2 (Data Link) — local MAC delivery is already working
explanation: A valid address rules out Layers 1 and 2, and a confirmed running service rules out Layer 7. That leaves routing to the remote network and whether the port is open and reachable.

prompt: Which TWO are true of IPv6 relative to IPv4?
choices: It uses 128-bit addresses, effectively eliminating address exhaustion
It supports stateless address autoconfiguration (SLAAC) without a DHCP server
It relies on broadcast traffic more heavily than IPv4
It requires NAT for every host to reach the internet
It reduces the address length to 16 bits
explanation: IPv6's 128-bit space and SLAAC are two of its defining features. IPv6 replaces broadcast with multicast, is designed to remove the need for NAT, and is far longer than IPv4, not shorter.

prompt: A design calls for a tunnel that both encapsulates traffic and encrypts it. Which TWO components together achieve this?
explanation: GRE tunnels traffic but provides no confidentiality, so it is routinely wrapped in IPsec, which supplies the encryption. CDN, QoS, and TTL serve entirely different purposes.

prompt: Which TWO cloud constructs let instances in a private subnet reach the internet for updates without being directly reachable from it?
choices: Route table entries directing outbound traffic to that gateway
An internet gateway attached directly to the private subnet
A network security list permitting all inbound traffic
Assigning every instance a public IP address
explanation: A NAT gateway plus routes pointing at it gives outbound-only access. Attaching an internet gateway, allowing all inbound, or assigning public IPs would all make the instances directly reachable — the opposite of the requirement.

prompt: Which TWO traffic types deliver a single sender's packets to more than one receiver?
explanation: Multicast reaches a subscribed group and broadcast reaches every host on the segment. Unicast is one-to-one, anycast routes to the single nearest advertiser, and loopback never leaves the host.

prompt: A technician is documenting which OSI layer defines connector pinouts, voltage levels, and how bits are represented as electrical or optical signals on the medium. Which layer is this?
explanation: The Physical layer covers everything about putting raw bits on the wire or fiber: connectors, pinouts, voltage and light levels, and signal encoding. It has no concept of addresses or frames.

prompt: What is the Protocol Data Unit at the Transport layer when TCP is in use?
explanation: TCP's PDU is the segment. UDP's is called a datagram, the Network layer's is a packet, and the Data Link layer's is a frame — the name changes at each layer as headers are added.

prompt: An old passive hub floods every incoming signal out all other ports with no awareness of MAC addresses. At which OSI layer does a hub operate?
explanation: A hub is a multiport repeater: it regenerates electrical signals without inspecting any header, so it works purely at the Physical layer. That is why every port on a hub shares one collision domain.

prompt: Which OSI layer is responsible for translating data into a format the application can use, including character encoding, compression, and encryption?
explanation: The Presentation layer handles data formatting and translation — character sets, compression, and encryption or decryption — so the receiving application sees data in a form it understands.

prompt: A packet is caught in a routing loop and its TTL field is decremented to zero. What does the router do?
choices: Discards the packet and may return an ICMP Time Exceeded message to the source
Forwards the packet one final time and then withdraws the route
Resets the TTL to its original value and continues forwarding
Fragments the packet so each piece receives a fresh TTL
explanation: Every router decrements TTL by one; at zero the packet is discarded and an ICMP Time Exceeded is typically sent back. This both stops routing loops and is the mechanism traceroute exploits to map a path.

prompt: A mail client submits outgoing messages to the organization's mail server over an encrypted connection negotiated with STARTTLS. Which port is the modern standard for authenticated mail submission?
explanation: Port 587 is the message submission port used by clients, normally with STARTTLS and authentication. Port 25 is reserved for server-to-server relay and is widely blocked outbound by ISPs to limit spam.

prompt: An application must query Active Directory over an encrypted LDAP connection. Which port should be permitted through the firewall?
explanation: LDAPS, which is LDAP wrapped in TLS, uses TCP 636. Plain unencrypted LDAP uses 389, which would expose directory queries and bind credentials to anyone capturing the traffic.

prompt: A monitoring server polls network devices for interface statistics, and those devices also send unsolicited alerts back when a link fails. Which port pair does SNMP use for these two directions?
choices: 161 for polling the agent, 162 for traps sent to the manager
162 for polling the agent, 161 for traps sent to the manager
explanation: The SNMP agent listens on UDP 161 for GET and SET requests from the manager. Traps and informs flow the other way, to the manager's UDP 162 — a distinction that matters when writing firewall rules in each direction.

prompt: A network team centralizes log messages from routers, switches, and firewalls onto a collector. Which default port does syslog use?
explanation: Syslog traditionally uses UDP 514. Because UDP has no delivery guarantee, busy networks sometimes use TCP 514 or TLS-protected 6514 instead so log messages are not silently lost.

prompt: A web application cannot reach its Microsoft SQL Server backend after a firewall change. Which default port should the technician verify is permitted?
explanation: Microsoft SQL Server listens on TCP 1433 by default. 3306 is MySQL, 1521 is Oracle, and 5432 is PostgreSQL — all common distractors on the exam.

prompt: An administrator connects to a Windows server's graphical desktop remotely. Which port must be reachable?
explanation: Remote Desktop Protocol uses TCP 3389. Port 5900 is VNC, 22 is SSH, and 23 is Telnet — RDP is the Microsoft-native graphical remote access protocol.

prompt: A VoIP deployment signals call setup and teardown using SIP, and the security team requires that signaling be encrypted with TLS. Which port carries SIP over TLS?
explanation: SIP uses 5060 in the clear and 5061 when secured with TLS. Note that SIP only handles signaling — the actual audio streams travel separately over RTP.

prompt: During a DHCP transaction, which UDP ports do the client and the server use?
choices: The client uses 68 and the server uses 67
The client uses 67 and the server uses 68
Both the client and the server use 67
The client uses 69 and the server uses 68
explanation: The DHCP server listens on UDP 67 and the client on UDP 68. Because the client has no address yet, the initial DISCOVER is broadcast from 0.0.0.0 to 255.255.255.255.

prompt: A data center patch panel uses a small fiber connector that holds two fibers in a single squeeze-latch housing, roughly half the width of the older square push-pull design. Which connector is this?
explanation: The LC, or Lucent Connector, is a small form factor connector, typically duplex, that allows much higher port density than SC. Its size is why LC is standard on SFP and SFP+ transceivers.

prompt: An older fiber installation uses a round connector secured with a spring-loaded bayonet twist-and-lock, carrying one fiber per connector. Which connector type is this?
explanation: The ST, or Straight Tip, connector uses a bayonet mount twisted a quarter turn to lock. It is a simplex connector, so a duplex link needs two of them, and it is mostly found in legacy multimode installations.

prompt: A technician terminates the coaxial drop from a cable internet provider onto a modem using a threaded screw-on connector. Which connector is this?
explanation: F-type connectors screw onto coax and are standard for cable television and cable modem service. BNC is a bayonet coax connector found in older 10BASE2 Ethernet and in video equipment.

prompt: How does an RJ11 connector differ physically from an RJ45?
choices: RJ11 is narrower and holds up to 6 positions, while RJ45 holds 8
RJ11 holds 8 positions and RJ45 holds 6
They are the same size but RJ11 is keyed differently
RJ11 is used for fiber and RJ45 for copper
explanation: RJ11 is a 6-position connector used for analog telephone lines and DSL; RJ45 is the wider 8-position connector used for Ethernet. An RJ11 plug will fit loosely into an RJ45 jack, which is a common wiring mistake.

prompt: A cabling contractor must run Ethernet through the space above a suspended ceiling that is also used to circulate return air for the building's HVAC system. What cable rating is required?
explanation: Plenum spaces circulate breathable air, so cable there must use a jacket that produces less smoke and fewer toxic fumes when burning. Plenum rating is a fire-code requirement, not a performance one.

prompt: A campus needs a copper run between two buildings, placed in a trench without conduit. What cable characteristic is required?
choices: A direct burial rating, with a gel-filled moisture barrier and rugged jacket
A plenum rating for fire safety
A riser rating for vertical shafts
A higher category rating such as Cat8
explanation: Direct burial cable is built with a heavy jacket and water-blocking compound to survive soil moisture, temperature swings, and crush forces. Note that fiber is often preferred between buildings anyway, to avoid ground potential differences.

prompt: A technician needs to build a crossover cable to connect two legacy devices directly. How should the ends be terminated?
choices: One end to T568A and the other to T568B
One end to T568B and the other reversed pin-for-pin, 8 to 1
explanation: Terminating one end A and the other B swaps the transmit and receive pairs, producing a crossover. Wiring both ends the same way makes a straight-through cable, and reversing all eight pins makes a rollover console cable.

prompt: An installer is planning 10GBASE-T runs of about 90 meters. Why is Cat6a specified rather than Cat6?
choices: Cat6 only supports 10 Gbps to roughly 55 meters, while Cat6a supports it to the full 100 meters
Cat6 cannot carry 10 Gbps at any distance
Cat6a is required for Power over Ethernet and Cat6 is not
Cat6 is not rated for installation inside walls
explanation: Both categories can carry 10 Gbps, but Cat6 is limited to about 55 meters, less in tightly bundled runs, because of alien crosstalk. Cat6a adds tighter twists and often shielding to hold 10 Gbps across a full 100 meter channel.

prompt: A data center needs 40 Gbps copper connections between top-of-rack switches and servers a few meters apart. Which cable category is designed for this short, high-speed role?
choices: Cat8, rated for 25 and 40 Gbps over roughly 30 meters
Cat5e, rated for 40 Gbps over 100 meters
Cat6, rated for 40 Gbps over 55 meters
Cat3, rated for high-frequency data center use
explanation: Cat8 pushes to 2 GHz to support 25GBASE-T and 40GBASE-T, but only to about 30 meters. That distance limit is why it is an in-rack data center cable rather than a horizontal building cable.

prompt: Two switches in the same rack are connected using a factory-assembled cable with transceivers permanently attached at both ends. What is this assembly called?
choices: A direct attach copper (DAC) twinax cable
explanation: A DAC twinax assembly bonds the cable and both transceivers into one unit. It is cheaper and lower-power than optics, but it is a fixed length and only works over a few meters.

prompt: How many usable host addresses does a 192.168.4.0/26 subnet provide?
explanation: A /26 leaves 6 host bits, giving 2^6 = 64 total addresses. Subtracting the network address and the broadcast address leaves 62 usable for hosts.

prompt: A host is configured with the address 172.16.35.200/21. What is the network address of its subnet?
explanation: A /21 mask is 255.255.248.0, so the third octet increments in blocks of 8: 32, 40, 48. The value 35 falls inside the block starting at 32, making 172.16.32.0 the network address.

prompt: A WAN link joins two routers and needs only the two router interface addresses. Which prefix length wastes the fewest addresses while still following classic subnetting rules?
explanation: A /30 provides four addresses: a network address, two usable host addresses, and a broadcast address — exactly right for a point-to-point pair. A /29 would waste six addresses on the same link.

prompt: Some modern point-to-point router links are configured with a /31 prefix. How is this possible when a /31 leaves no room for a network or broadcast address?
choices: RFC 3021 allows both addresses in a /31 to be used as host addresses on point-to-point links
The router silently borrows an address from the neighboring subnet
A /31 automatically expands to a /30 when applied to a serial interface
Broadcast traffic is disabled globally whenever a /31 is configured
explanation: On a point-to-point link there is only ever one possible destination, so broadcast has no meaning and RFC 3021 permits using both addresses as hosts. This halves the address consumption of WAN links compared with /30.

prompt: What is the broadcast address of the subnet 10.10.8.0/22?
explanation: A /22 mask means the third octet increments in blocks of 4, so this subnet spans 10.10.8.0 through 10.10.11.255. The last address in that range, 10.10.11.255, is the broadcast address.

prompt: A workstation shows the address 169.254.18.7 with mask 255.255.0.0 and no default gateway. What does this indicate?
choices: The client could not reach a DHCP server and self-assigned an APIPA address
The client received a valid lease from a DHCP server on a different subnet
The client has been assigned a public routable address
The client's IPv6 stack has taken over from IPv4
explanation: The 169.254.0.0/16 range is APIPA, self-assigned when DHCP fails. It permits communication with other APIPA hosts on the same segment but provides no gateway, so nothing beyond the local link is reachable.

prompt: A host needs the MAC address matching an IPv4 address on its own subnet, so it sends an ARP request. Which traffic type does that request use?
explanation: An ARP request is broadcast to ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff because the sender does not yet know which host owns the address. The reply comes back as a unicast directly to the requester.

prompt: An organization places a device in front of its own web servers to terminate TLS, cache responses, and hide the real server addresses from clients. What is this device acting as?
explanation: A reverse proxy sits in front of servers and answers on their behalf, so clients never contact the origin directly. A forward proxy does the opposite job, sitting in front of clients to control and cache their outbound requests.

prompt: A load balancer distributes requests across a pool of web servers, but a shopping cart application breaks when a user's requests land on different servers mid-session. Which load balancer feature resolves this?
choices: Session persistence, also called sticky sessions
Health checking of the server pool
explanation: Session persistence pins a client to the same backend server for the life of their session, usually by cookie or source address. Without it, an application storing state locally on one server loses that state when the next request is balanced elsewhere.

prompt: What is the fundamental difference between network attached storage (NAS) and a storage area network (SAN)?
choices: NAS presents shared storage at the file level, while a SAN presents raw block-level volumes to servers
NAS presents block-level volumes, while a SAN presents file shares
NAS is always faster than a SAN because it avoids Ethernet
A SAN can only be built with iSCSI, and NAS only with Fibre Channel
explanation: NAS speaks file protocols such as SMB and NFS and appears as a network share. A SAN delivers raw block devices over Fibre Channel or iSCSI that a server formats as if they were local disks.

prompt: Several unrelated customer organizations run workloads on the same underlying cloud provider hardware, logically isolated from one another. What is this property called?
explanation: Multitenancy means one physical infrastructure serves many independent tenants with logical separation. It is what makes public cloud economics work, and it is also why isolation controls matter so much there.

prompt: A cloud workload automatically adds instances during a traffic spike and removes them an hour later when demand drops. Which cloud characteristic does this describe?
explanation: Elasticity is the ability to expand and, critically, contract capacity automatically as demand changes. Scalability describes the capacity to grow, but elasticity emphasises that resources are released again when no longer needed.

prompt: A cloud engineer attaches a stateful rule set to a virtual machine's interface that permits inbound TCP 443 and denies everything else. What is this construct generally called?
explanation: Network security groups act as stateful virtual firewalls attached to instances or interfaces. Because they are stateful, permitting an inbound request automatically allows the matching return traffic.

prompt: Several hospitals with identical regulatory requirements jointly fund and share a cloud environment restricted to their group. Which deployment model is this?
explanation: A community cloud is shared by organizations with common concerns such as compliance or mission, splitting cost while keeping outsiders out. It sits between a private cloud's exclusivity and a public cloud's open tenancy.

prompt: In a three-tier hierarchical campus design, what is the role of the access layer?
choices: Connecting end devices to the network and enforcing port-level policy
Aggregating access switches and applying routing policy between them
Providing high-speed backbone forwarding between distribution blocks
Terminating the organization's internet and WAN circuits
explanation: The access layer is where end devices plug in, so it handles port security, PoE, and VLAN assignment. Distribution aggregates and applies policy, while core forwards traffic between distribution blocks as fast as possible.

prompt: A switch uplink must run at 10 Gbps over multimode fiber. Which transceiver form factor is appropriate?
explanation: SFP+ is the 10 Gbps evolution of the 1 Gbps SFP, in the same physical footprint. QSFP+ is the quad form factor used for 40 Gbps, effectively four 10 Gbps lanes in one module.

prompt: A technician is classifying protocols by OSI layer for a design document. Which TWO of the following operate at the Transport layer?
explanation: TCP and UDP are the two Transport layer protocols, distinguished by port numbers. ICMP and GRE ride directly on IP at the Network layer, and ARP maps addresses at the Data Link boundary.

prompt: A firewall rule must allow a mail client to retrieve mail with IMAP over TLS and submit outgoing mail securely. Which TWO ports are required?
explanation: IMAP over TLS uses 993 and authenticated submission uses 587. Ports 143 and 110 are the unencrypted IMAP and POP3 equivalents, and 25 is server-to-server relay rather than client submission.

prompt: A PAT-enabled router translates an internal host's outbound web session. Which TWO header fields does it rewrite on the way out?
choices: The MAC address of the original host
explanation: PAT rewrites the source IP to the router's public address and the source port to a unique value, so many internal hosts can share one public address. The destination fields must stay intact or the packet would never reach the intended server.

prompt: Which TWO properties of UDP make it the preferred transport for live voice traffic?
choices: It has no connection setup handshake, so there is less startup delay
It does not retransmit lost packets, avoiding delay from late-arriving audio
It guarantees in-order delivery of every packet
It dynamically reduces its sending rate whenever loss is detected
explanation: For live audio a packet that arrives late is worse than one that never arrives at all, so UDP's lack of handshake and retransmission is a feature. Guaranteed ordering and congestion backoff are TCP behaviours, and neither transport encrypts on its own.

prompt: Which TWO devices make their forwarding decisions using MAC addresses?
explanation: Switches and bridges both build a MAC address table and forward frames at Layer 2. Routers forward on IP addresses at Layer 3, while hubs and media converters simply repeat or convert signals with no addressing awareness.

prompt: A network team moves device provisioning to infrastructure as code. Which TWO benefits does this directly provide?
choices: Deployments become repeatable, producing identical configurations every time
Configuration changes are version controlled, so they can be reviewed and rolled back
Physical cabling errors are automatically detected and corrected
Bandwidth on existing WAN circuits increases
Encryption is automatically applied to all management traffic
explanation: Defining infrastructure as code removes the configuration drift that comes from manual changes, and puts every change under source control with history and review. It says nothing about physical media, link capacity, or encryption.

prompt: A user reports no network access. Which TWO observations together indicate the workstation failed to obtain a DHCP lease?
choices: No default gateway is listed in the IP configuration
The address is within the 10.0.0.0/8 range
The DNS suffix matches the corporate domain
The interface reports a 1 Gbps link speed
explanation: An APIPA address in 169.254.0.0/16 combined with no default gateway is the signature of DHCP failure, because APIPA self-assignment never provides gateway or DNS settings. A 10.x address and a correct DNS suffix would indicate the opposite.

prompt: Match each connector to its description.

pairs.right: A compact fiber connector with a squeeze latch, usually duplex, standard on SFP modules
A round simplex fiber connector locked with a bayonet twist
A rectangular fiber connector carrying twelve or more strands in one ferrule
A threaded screw-on connector used to terminate coaxial cable

explanation: Connector recognition is a common exam task. LC is the small duplex fiber connector on SFPs, ST twists to lock, MPO bundles many fibers for high-density trunks, and F-type screws onto coax for cable service.

prompt: Match each copper cable category to the speed and distance it supports.
explanation: Category ratings pair a speed with a maximum distance, and the distance is what usually gets forgotten. Cat6 supports 10 Gbps only on short runs, Cat6a extends that to a full channel, and Cat8 trades distance for very high data center speeds.
